record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Determine whether the guaranteed α-value in the α-diamond-property analysis of minimum-weight triangulations can be improved beyond π/8.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9. Is the α-value for minimum weight triangulations greater than π/8?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane in general position. A triangulation of $P$ is a maximal planar straight-line graph whose vertex set is $P$. The minimum-weight triangulation $MWT(P)$ is the triangulation of $P$ minimizing the total Euclidean length of its edges.

For an angle $\alpha \in (0, \pi/2)$, a straight-line edge $e = uv$ is said to have the $\alpha$-diamond property (with respect to $P$) if at least one of the two isosceles triangles having $e$ as a base and base angle $\alpha$ contains no point of $P \setminus \{u,v\}$ in its interior. A planar graph $G$ on $P$ has the $\alpha$-diamond property if every edge of $G$ has it. It is known that any planar graph on $P$ whose edges all satisfy the $\alpha$-diamond property is a geometric spanner of the complete Euclidean graph on $P$, with stretch factor bounded by a function of $\alpha$ alone.

It is known that every edge of $MWT(P)$ satisfies the $\alpha$-diamond property for $\alpha = \pi/8$. Determine the largest value of $\alpha$ such that every edge of every minimum-weight triangulation of every finite planar point set $P$ in general position is guaranteed to satisfy the $\alpha$-diamond property. In particular, decide whether this largest value strictly exceeds $\pi/8$.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has improved the diamond-property angle guaranteed by minimum-weight triangulations beyond π/8: Drysdale, McElfresh, and Snoeyink improved the angle to roughly π/4.6, and related works (Das–Joseph; Cheng–Xu, etc.) further refined diamond-property analyses. However, the exact largest angle α for which every edge of every MWT is guaranteed to have the α-diamond property does not appear to be settled, so the problem is partially resolved rather than fully closed.

status_evidence.snippet: Every edge in a minimum weight triangulation has the diamond property... The angle was later improved to π/4.6 by Drysdale et al.
status_evidence.claim: The π/8 bound has been improved to roughly π/4.6, so the α-value strictly exceeds π/8.

status_evidence.claim: There are known limitations to how strong the diamond property can be for MWT, indicating the exact optimal α is not fully determined.
